explanation: A holy place where Jews performed religious ceremonies and sacrifices to God.
Members of the tribe of Levi who had special religious duties in the temple, including music, singing, and assisting the priests.
Religious leaders from the line of Aaron who were responsible for performing sacrifices and other ceremonies in the temple.
A Jewish leader and governor in Jerusalem who helped rebuild the city's walls and reform religious life after the exile in Babylon.
The period when the Jews were taken captive and lived in Babylon after Jerusalem was destroyed by the Babylonians.
The process of repairing and reconstructing the walls and temple of Jerusalem after the exile.
The ceremony where the temple and walls of Jerusalem were consecrated and dedicated to God after the rebuilding.
A religious song or hymn expressing gratitude, reverence, and praise to God.
